name: Lake Kol-Tor
near: Kegety dachas and the tourist bases/guesthouses in the gorge (trailhead); Kegety village — ~11 km below the trailhead (asia-hikes); Bishkek — 82–90 km.
elev: About 2700–2735 m: 2725 m (thegonegoat), 2733 m (asia-hikes), ~2700 m (pinyourfootsteps, the previous entry).
short: Kol-Tor is a turquoise glacial-moraine lake at ~2730 m in a side valley of the Kegety gorge, 82–90 km from Bishkek; one of the most popular day hikes from the capital.
desc: Kol-Tor (Kyol-Tyor, Kel-Tor) is a lake of glacial-moraine origin above the tree line (bookit.kg) in the valley of the same name, a side valley of the Kegety gorge on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too. The water is bright turquoise and very cold all year round. From the parking in the gorge, a 7–8 km trail climbs 800–1000 m through spruce forest, along a stream and up steep switchbacks (hiking.kg: 7.5 km, 3.5 h, +1000 m). At the start there are guesthouses and a Trekking Union hut; you can pitch a tent beyond the lake. In summer, organized day groups come here from Bishkek (Trekking Union, Kyrgyz Concept, ticket.kg).
guide: Kol-Tor is a classic day hike from Bishkek: set out at 6–7 am so you start the climb before the heat. The hardest stretch is the steep switchbacks after the forest; after that the trail reaches the moraine, and the lake suddenly opens up in bright turquoise. We don't recommend swimming — the water is icy all year, and the wind at the lake is often strong. If you want some quiet, stay overnight in a guesthouse at the trailhead or camp beyond the lake. It's best to head back with time to spare: finding transport out of the gorge in the evening is almost impossible.
see: The turquoise moraine lake and the glacial slopes above it; spruce forests and the stream in the Kol-Tor valley along the way; panoramas of the Kegety gorge; in the gorge itself, Kegety Waterfall (separate entry, 4.9 km).
skip: You aren't ready for a climb of 800–1000 m in one day (7–8 km each way, 6–8 h in total). You have no car or tour — it's hard to get out of the gorge by public transport. You're looking for solitude on a summer weekend — the trail has many groups from Bishkek.
diff: A physically demanding hike: 7.5 km one way, about 1000 m of ascent, 3.5 h up (hiking.kg — difficulty 4/5); other sources say 800–900 m of ascent and 3–5 h (pinyourfootsteps, thegonegoat). Steep switchbacks, stream fords; slippery in wet weather, ice in winter — you need crampons (asia-hikes).
when: July–August is optimal (hiking.kg); the season overall is May to October, outside it the trail is under snow, hard and dangerous (pinyourfootsteps). In winter people hike with crampons (asia-hikes); in mid-October there may be deep snow.
hours: A natural site with no schedule. The post/barrier at the entrance to the Kegety gorge (eco fee) operates in daylight — hours not confirmed.
daytime: Start the climb early in the morning (7–9 am): it's cool on the ascent, in the morning the lake is usually calm and brighter in color, while in the afternoon there is more often wind and cloud (editorial; wind — asia-hikes).
how: By car: Bishkek → Krasnaya Rechka → Yuryevka → Syn-Tash → Rot-Front → Kegety gorge, after the first bridge at the fork go straight on toward the Kol-Tor valley, then on foot (hiking.kg). Public transport: a marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek's Eastern Bus Station to Kegety village (about 2 h; 50 som per thegonegoat 2024 — the price is probably outdated), then ~11 km by hitching/on foot to the trailhead (asia-hikes).
needcar: Yes: your own car, a taxi or an organized tour. The marshrutka goes only as far as the village; the remaining ~11 km up the gorge are on foot or by hitching; finding transport back is very hard (thegonegoat).
self: Yes: no permits needed, the trail is popular and well trodden. At the entrance to the gorge an eco fee is charged per car. Without mountain hiking experience it's better to go with a group.
roadtype: Paved road gives way to a dirt road at Kegety; the last driveable section is rough. A trail leads to the lake.
traveltime: Hiking.kg reference: from Bishkek to the trailhead 82 km / 2 h 10 min; from the parking to the lake 7.5 km / 3.5 h, ascent about 1000 m. On foot there and back 7–8 h.
stay: At the trailhead: Kegety Tour guesthouse (~1 km to the start, 1500 som/person with three meals a day — asia-hikes), the Kol-Tor guesthouse (Booking, 25 reviews), the Trekking Union hut (book via TUK — thegonegoat), Malinka (pinyourfootsteps); tent spots at the trailhead and beyond the lake.
net: The source notes a rare signal at the guesthouse and no stable coverage at the lake; operators are not specified.
entry: The eco fee at the post in the Kegety gorge is about 200 som per car (hiking.kg, 2024); the current amount for 2026 is not confirmed. There is no separate fee for the lake.
transfer: Trekking Union tour ~450 som/person with transport (thegonegoat, 2024); marshrutka to Kegety 50 som (2024, probably outdated — for comparison: Tokmok — Krasnaya Rechka 60 som, Kaktus 02.2026). A taxi price Bishkek — Kol-Tor for 2025–2026 was not found.
bring: Trekking shoes, 1.5–2 L of water and food for the whole day (there are no shops on the trail or at the start — stock up at a supermarket on the way), a warm windproof jacket, sun protection, an offline map; in winter — crampons; for an overnight stay — a warm sleeping bag (cold nights — thegonegoat).
warn: 800–1000 m of ascent in a day to an elevation of ~2730 m — gauge your strength and time, and turn back if the weather worsens. Outside May to October the trail is under snow and dangerous, and in winter crampons are needed on icy sections (pinyourfootsteps, asia-hikes). The lake water is icy all year — swimming is dangerous. The wind at the lake is strong — secure your tent. In the evening it is almost impossible to find transport out of the gorge — arrange a return car in advance. No signal at the lake.
food: At the start — guesthouses with meals (Kegety Tour — 1500 som/person with a bed and three meals a day, asia-hikes; the guesthouse has instant coffee and simple dishes, pinyourfootsteps). There is no food on the trail or at the lake — stock up at a supermarket on the way.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 88 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). Booking: Kol-Tor guesthouse — 25 reviews. Pros: the color of the lake, closeness to Bishkek, views; cons: the steep climb, cold and wind at the lake, difficult return transport.
p.sum: Kol-Tor is a classic day hike from Bishkek: by car via Krasnaya Rechka — Yuryevka — Rot-Front into the Kegety gorge (≈82–90 km, ≈2 h), after the first bridge straight on into the Kol-Tor valley to the guesthouse/yurts at the start, where you leave the car; then 7.5 km and +800–1000 m on a well-trodden trail (3–3.5 h up, 2–2.5 h down). Without a car the easiest options are a group tour (Trekking Union and others), a taxi to the start ≈1500 som, or marshrutka (minibus) No. 303 from the Eastern Bus Station to Kegety village (09:30 and 15:30, ≈80 som) + 11 km by hitching. Set out before 8–9 am and arrange a return car in advance; bring water and food — there is nothing at the lake.

p.iti.0.title: 1 day from Bishkek by car
p.iti.0.plan: 06:00 depart → 08:15 parking at the guesthouse → 08:30 start → 11:30 the lake, a snack → 12:30 descent → 15:00 back at the car → optionally 15:30 Kegety Waterfall (5 min from the road) → 18:30 Bishkek.
p.iti.1.title: 2 days with an overnight
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: arrive at the guesthouse after lunch (Kegety Tour/Sun City), evening by the river. Day 2: an early climb to the lake in calm weather, descent, Kegety Waterfall and Burana on the way to Bishkek.
p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Kol-Tor + Kegety Waterfall (the same gorge); + Burana (via Tokmok, ≈1 h); + Issyk-Ata gorge (the next one to the west).
p.season: May–June: snow patches on the switchbacks, full fords. July–August is optimal, the brightest color, weekends have many groups. September–October: quiet, cold, deep snow possible in mid-October. November–April: the trail is under snow and ice, crampons needed, avalanche-prone; the lake is under ice.
p.budget.economy: ≈700–1500 som/person: TUK tour ≈450 som (2024) or marshrutka No. 303 2×80 + hitching; food from home 300–500; a night in a guesthouse with meals 1500.
p.budget.comfort: ≈3000–6000 som/person: taxi ≈1500 som one way (per group) or a crossover rental $65–100/day; a night at Tazabek/Sun City; a combo tour with Burana.
p.permits: No permit needed. At the post at the entrance to the Kegety gorge an eco fee of ≈200 som per car is sometimes charged (hiking.kg 2024); other sources say entry is free — keep cash.
p.access: With children — only hardy ones from about 10 years old (800–1000 m climb); hard for older people; stroller — no; with a dog — allowed (Toodo accepts pets), keep it at heel on the trail because of livestock.
